newsitem.title: THAILAND: Morgan Stanley asks market to wait for rates cut.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley asks market to wait for rates cut.

text.p: Morgan Stanley Dean Witter (Thailand) on Friday advised investors to wait for real Thai interest rates to ease at least 150 basis points before raising their exposure in Thailand.

"We think the Thai stock market is quite close to the bottom now. However, we've recommended to investors that they wait for a significant decline in real interest rates, by 150 basis points or more, before increasing their exposure," Nikhil Srinivasan, vice president of Morgan Stanley Asia Ltd, told a seminar.
Battered Thai stocks plunged to 97-month lows this week, weakened by market concerns over the ailing Thai economy, sour property loans extended by finance firms, and high interest rates.
Currency control measures adopted by the central bank this week aggravated the market weakness and kept foreign investors further on the sidelines.
Current Thai prime lending rates of 12.75-13.50 percent are among the highest in South East Asia.
Srinivasan said although the Thai bourse has suffered heavy losses, it is still weighed by uncertain government policy and currency control measures.
"I think these currency control measures would be for short-term. People are just waiting for clarity on currency policy and clarification of government policy in a longer term," he said.
Kulpatra Sirodom, adviser of Securities One Plc, said investors were more keen to buy medium and small stocks as they posed less risks than blue-chips.
"Some of these stocks have good prospects but it's difficult to buy due to their lack of liquidity. We also believe that they are being held by company owners," Kulpatra said.
